content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The key constructive step of the refinement lemma's upper bound (Xiang's overlay cuts realizing D=\u0393 within q-1 cuts) is asserted as \"standard; details omitted\", including the tight cut count.", "errors": [{"description": "The heart of Xiang's explicit strategy \u2014 overlaying the A-row and B-row, taking the common refinement, and checking that the total number of new cuts (including the cut at the point corresponding to s_B, which makes the bound exactly q-1 and hence tight) is at most q-1 \u2014 is not carried out. The reconstruction is routine but the count is delicate and unverified.", "quote": "and use at most \\(q-1\\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted)."}, {"description": "The \"grid example\" is claimed to agree with the theorem, but for Liu's split (7,14,35)/56 one has \u0393 = 7/56 = 1/8, so the game value of that split is 9/16, not 4/7; Xiang's marks (8,38) are suboptimal. The agreement is coincidental. (Flagged as evidence, not proof, so harmless.)", "quote": "Sorting gives Liu\n\\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\\), in agreement with the theorem."}, {"description": "Sections 5\u20136 are largely extraneous (falsification log, references to scripts) and do not contribute to the argument; the assertion that a Liu mark coinciding with an overlay boundary \"only reduce[s] the cut count\" is stated without checking it cannot also destroy the pairing structure (it does not, but this is unargued).", "quote": "An overlay boundary already equal to a Liu mark requires no new mark, so\ncoincidences only reduce the cut count."}], "notes": "Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) checks out; greedy drafting lemma, the tree/bipartition lower bound D \u2265 \u0393, and the subset-sum pigeonhole are all correct and rigorously done. Only the constructive half of the refinement lemma is sketched."}
